newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO sees Peru copper expansion on track.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO sees Peru copper expansion on track.

text.p: ASARCO said the money needed to fund a billion dollar expansion at its Southern Peru Copper Corp majority-owned subsidiary will be available without raising equity, the company told an analyst briefing.
Richard de J Osborne said corporate funding will be used to pay for the expansion of its Cuajone mine and modernising the Ilo smelter in Peru.
"We have received attractive financing proposals. We now believe the required finance will be available," Osborne said.
The entire assets of SPCC will support the financing.
"ASARCO will provide no guarantees. SPCC will stand on its own. It has a very strong balance sheet," Osborne said.

The first approved expansion stage will spend $245 million to raise total copper production at Cuajone by 26 percent. Construction will start in 1997 and expanded output will start coming on stream in 1999.

In the second, $787 million stage, only the engineering for the modernisation of the Ilo smelter has been approved. Start-up would be in 2001 to eventually capture 95 percent of the sulphur emissions.
Cuajone has enough reserves to continue operating at existing levels for 55 years.
